terminology_registry.source_meaning: A relationship that makes an action possible for a person in context.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: An affordance is not the mark, label, or cue that advertises the action.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Check whether the action is actually possible, not merely labeled.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not call every visual cue an affordance.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: The revised edition sharpens the affordance/signifier separation.

terminology_registry.important_distinction: A signifier communicates; it does not by itself create the action possibility.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Check labels, placement, shape, state, and conventions that tell people what to do.

terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Signifier is central in the revised edition.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The ability to determine what actions are possible and what state exists.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Visibility may expose elements; discoverability requires usable meaning for action.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Observe whether people can identify the next valid action without instructions.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not equate a visible button with a discoverable action.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Highlighted in the revised edition as a fundamental principle.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: Perceptual availability of relevant actions, objects, and state.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Visibility is a contributor to discoverability, not the whole diagnostic category.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Inspect whether important state and available actions can be seen at the time of need.

source_traceability.author: Don Norman

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for visibility.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The user can make sense of how the system works and what results mean.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Discoverability is about finding possible action; understanding is about interpreting operation and outcome.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Ask users to predict what an action will do and explain what happened afterward.

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Understanding concerns whether people can interpret meaning, operation, and results.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for understanding.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: Information returned after action that tells what happened and supports evaluation.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Confirmation asks permission or acknowledgement; feedback reports action/result/state.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Specify timing, content, target, and next step for the feedback.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not use a generic spinner when the user needs status or result details.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for feedback.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A pre-action or transitional check used when commitment or consequence matters.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Confirmation is not a substitute for showing actual result after action.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Use it selectively where reversibility is low or intent is ambiguous.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not add confirmation dialogs to every action.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Design can reduce the chance and cost of error.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for confirmation.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The relationship between controls, action choices, and their effects.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: A label can name an action; mapping lets users predict which action produces which effect.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Test whether people can predict an effect from control position, order, and naming.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not solve a mapping problem with only longer instructions.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A mapping that uses spatial, cultural, or perceptual correspondences to make action-effect relations easier to infer.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Natural mapping is about correspondence, not just consistent vocabulary.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Arrange controls so the structure suggests the effect.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not call arbitrary order natural because it is familiar to the designer.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

directly_supported_claims: Natural mappings can reduce memory and make control-effect relationships easier to infer.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for natural mapping.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A design limitation that narrows possible actions or states.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: A constraint changes what can happen; a warning merely asks the user to comply.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Identify invalid states the design can make impossible.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not rely on warnings when the system can prevent the error.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip

source_traceability.author: Don Norman

directly_supported_claims: Constraints reduce the set of possible actions.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for constraint.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A limitation imposed by physical shape, size, position, or incompatibility.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Physical constraints work through fit and possibility rather than meaning.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Use shape or compatibility to prevent wrong assembly or wrong selection where possible.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not describe a policy rule as a physical constraint.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.chapter_title: Knowing What to Do: Constraints, Discoverability, and Feedback
directly_supported_claims: Physical constraints restrict possible physical actions.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for physical constraint.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A limitation based on learned social conventions and expectations.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Cultural constraints depend on shared conventions and may vary by population.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Validate icon, color, order, and gesture meanings with the target user group.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not assume the designer’s convention is universal.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.chapter_title: Knowing What to Do: Constraints, Discoverability, and Feedback
directly_supported_claims: Cultural constraints rely on learned conventions.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for cultural constraint.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A limitation based on the meaning of a situation and what actions make sense in it.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Semantic constraints use meaning; logical constraints use relations among remaining possibilities.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Ask what actions the task meaning itself rules out.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not use semantic explanations when users lack the domain meaning.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.chapter_title: Knowing What to Do: Constraints, Discoverability, and Feedback
directly_supported_claims: Semantic constraints use meaning to limit plausible actions.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for semantic constraint.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A limitation inferred from relationships among components, choices, or remaining possibilities.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Logical constraints rely on relational structure rather than social convention or task meaning alone.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Show completeness, one-to-one correspondence, and remaining unmatched items.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not hide the set of remaining possibilities.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.chapter_title: Knowing What to Do: Constraints, Discoverability, and Feedback
directly_supported_claims: Logical constraints use relations among choices to limit possibilities.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for logical constraint.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: An explanatory model of how something works that supports prediction and action.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: The designed or communicated conceptual model is not identical to what a user actually believes.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Check whether the interface teaches the right operating idea.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not expose implementation details and call that a conceptual model.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Conceptual models help people predict what actions are possible and how the system will respond.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for conceptual model.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The user’s internal belief about how a system works.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Mental model is the user’s belief; conceptual model may be the designer’s intended explanation.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Elicit user predictions to detect mismatch.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not infer a mental model from one click without evidence.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: People form internal models from interaction, explanation, and experience.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for mental model.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The total perceivable evidence from which users infer the system’s operation.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: The interface is part of the system image, but the system image includes behavior, labels, documentation, feedback, and results.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Audit what the system communicates through all user-facing signals.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not assume the designer’s model reaches users unless the system image communicates it.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: The system image is what users can infer from the perceivable design and communication.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for system image.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: Remembered knowledge carried by the user.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Head knowledge can be efficient but is fragile under interruption, rarity, and stress.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Identify what people must memorize to complete the task.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not remove every memory demand; learned expertise can be valuable.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.chapter_title: Knowledge in the Head and in the World
directly_supported_claims: Knowledge in the head can be efficient when learned, but it depends on memory and practice.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for knowledge in the head.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: Information embedded in the environment, artifact, labels, layout, state, examples, or constraints.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: World knowledge reduces memorization but can be slower or cluttering if overused.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Move fragile steps, state, and prerequisites into visible cues.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not confuse documentation hidden elsewhere with usable world knowledge.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.chapter_title: Knowledge in the Head and in the World
directly_supported_claims: Knowledge in the world can reduce dependence on remembered information.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for knowledge in the world.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: Forming and carrying out actions that move from a goal to interaction.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Execution asks how to do it; evaluation asks what happened.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Diagnose whether the user can choose and perform the next action.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not repair execution failures only with success messages.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: The gulf of execution concerns forming and carrying out an action to meet a goal.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for execution.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: Perceiving and interpreting the system state after action.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Evaluation is about sensemaking after action, not choosing the action.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Check whether outcome, status, meaning, and next step are visible.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not treat completion as clear if the user cannot interpret the result.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: The gulf of evaluation concerns perceiving and interpreting system state after action.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for evaluation.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The gap between a person’s goal and the actions the design makes available or understandable.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Execution gap precedes or occurs during action choice and performance.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Ask what the user wants to do and which action appears to do it.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not misclassify a result-interpretation problem as execution.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.section_heading: The Gulfs of Execution and Evaluation
directly_supported_claims: The gulf of execution describes difficulty translating goals into actions.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for gulf of execution.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The gap between system output/state and the user’s ability to interpret it.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Evaluation gap appears when the user cannot tell what happened or what it means.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Observe repeated checking, duplicate action, or requests for status meaning.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not assume feedback solved evaluation if it lacks interpretable content.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.author: Don Norman
source_traceability.section_heading: The Gulfs of Execution and Evaluation
directly_supported_claims: The gulf of evaluation describes difficulty interpreting system state and results.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for gulf of evaluation.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: An error in which the intention is appropriate but the action or memory execution fails.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Slip diagnosis focuses on execution, attention, habit, memory, and target discrimination.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Ask whether the user knew what they wanted to do before the failure.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not prescribe conceptual training for a simple target-selection slip.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Slips occur when the goal is correct but execution or memory fails.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for slip.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: An error in which the goal, plan, or interpretation is wrong.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Mistake diagnosis focuses on knowledge, rules, and conceptual model, not motor execution alone.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Ask what rule or understanding led to the action.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not treat every wrong action as a slip.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Mistakes occur when the goal or plan is wrong because the situation is misunderstood.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for mistake.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A frequent habitual sequence captures a less frequent intended sequence after a shared beginning.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Capture is sequence/habit dominance; description-similarity is wrong target similarity.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Look for actions that begin correctly and then veer into a more practiced routine.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not blame carelessness when design lets routine overpower intention.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Capture slips occur when a familiar sequence takes over a less familiar intended sequence.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for capture slip.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The wrong target is chosen because it resembles the intended target in appearance, description, or location.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: The failure is target discrimination, not habitual sequence takeover.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Increase perceptual and semantic separation between confusable targets.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not solve target similarity only with training.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Description-similarity slips involve choosing a wrong item that matches the intended description.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for description-similarity slip.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: The same action has different meanings in different states or modes, and the user acts under the wrong assumed mode.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Mode error depends on hidden or misunderstood state-dependent meanings.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Make mode visible, reduce mode dependence, or make actions mode-independent.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not rely on memory of mode when consequence is high.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Mode errors occur when actions are interpreted differently in different modes.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for mode error.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A planned action, step, or goal is forgotten during execution, often after interruption.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: A lapse can occur despite a correct plan; it is not necessarily misunderstanding.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Support resumption, checkpoints, and visible sequence state.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not assume the user never learned the task.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Memory lapses involve forgetting intended actions or steps.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for memory-lapse slip/error.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A known rule is selected or applied incorrectly.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: The user has a rule, but it is the wrong rule for this situation or is misapplied.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Improve discrimination cues and rule-condition visibility.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not over-explain the whole system when the rule cue is the failure.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Rule-based mistakes involve misuse or misselection of rules.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for rule-based mistake.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A novel or poorly understood situation is handled through incomplete reasoning or a weak model.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: The user lacks an adequate rule/model rather than merely choosing the wrong known rule.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Strengthen conceptual model, examples, and interpretable feedback.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not blame lack of attention when the situation is genuinely novel.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Knowledge-based mistakes arise in situations where reasoning from knowledge is required.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for knowledge-based mistake.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A design that prevents progress unless required conditions are satisfied.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: A forcing function changes the action path rather than merely cautioning.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Use when missing a condition creates serious error or rework.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not overuse forcing functions where they create needless blockage.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Forcing functions constrain action so that required conditions must be met before progress.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for forcing function.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A forcing function that keeps an operation active until it is safe or complete to stop.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Lock-in preserves required continuation; lockout blocks entry or action.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Use where premature exit would cause loss or danger.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not trap users without a safe recovery route.
terminology_registry.edition_specific_note: Terminology reviewed against the uploaded revised edition.

source_traceability.source_file: The Design of Everyday Things Revised and Expanded Edition.epub(1).zip
source_traceability.book_title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
source_traceability.author: Don Norman
directly_supported_claims: Lock-in is a type of forcing function.

derivation.explanation: Terminology record preserves the edition-specific distinction for lock-in.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A forcing function that prevents entry into an unsafe or invalid state.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Lockout prevents an action; lock-in prevents premature discontinuation.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Use to block actions that should not be available under current conditions.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A forcing function requiring a safe sequence or condition before another action can proceed.
terminology_registry.important_distinction: Interlock enforces sequence; confirmation asks for acknowledgment.
terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Use when ordering matters and wrong order causes harm or unrecoverable failure.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not use an interlock when simple feedback would be enough.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: A design approach grounded in people’s needs, abilities, behavior, and context.

terminology_registry.observable_design_implication: Observe real work and test prototypes against actual behavior.
terminology_registry.misuse_warning: Do not call a design human-centered because it is aesthetically preferred.

terminology_registry.source_meaning: Automation can make routine work easier while making rare failures harder to detect, understand, and recover from.
